sentences.text: The appellant has stated in the appeal that MMTC-V Court has not applied the mind and passed the impugned order.
The trial Court has no evidence or proof for passing impugned orders, hence the same deserves to be set aside.
The respondent is not eligible for any interim orders for maintenance as she has neglected aged parents of the appellant, pressurized to make separate house.
The appellant is uneducated, without employment and no property of his own, even then it has arbitrarily allowed the application.

The appellant further stated that he is suffering from mental ill-health, even today, take treatment from the Hospital, he is working in cooli and now getting income of Rs.8,000/- per month, out of which he has to maintain his old aged parents, they are suffering from multiple ailments i.e., Sugar, B.P., and other deceases attack to them and his basic needs like food, clothing and medicines and other expenses.
The Court has hurriedly disposed the application and has overlooked the Assets and Liability affidavits filed by both the parties.
Therefore he prays to set aside the order passed by the learned MMTC-V, Bengaluru.
3. In pursuance of the notice, the respondent appeared through her counsel and filed objections to the appeal.
4. The respondent contended in the objections that the appeal along with written argument is not maintainable in law or on facts and as such it is liable to be dismissed in limine.
The appellant has made false, vexatious and malafide allegations against the respondent and an attempt to abuse the process of law and to harass the respondent.

The respondent submits that the appellant is legally wedded husband of the respondent having married on 3.5.2017 at Sarakari Naukara Bhavan, behind Fire Brigade Office, Hassan Road, Chanarayapatna, the said marriage was arranged marriage, the entire expenses were borne by the respondent parents.

Out of their wedlock a female child viz.,
Yoshitha M born on 17.09.2018.
After the marriage they both lead their life in and they have stayed at Vidyanagar, Chanarayapatna in the month of June- 2017.

The appellant is running business in the name of Dhanya Shri Auto Links and earning Rs.80,000/- per month and having 4 acres of coconut yielding farm and 1 acre dry land at Y-Singenahalli and earning an amount of Rs.2,00,000/-.
Further, he is having two residential sites in Channarayapatna town.
After marriage they lived happily for some days.
The appellant is having negative thinking and very adamant in speaking with respondent and her parents.
The appellant harassed the respondent physically and mentally.
Whenever the appellant go out of the house, he used to lock the house from outside.
Then the respondent moved to her parent's house.
The appellant demanded to bring Rs.10,00,000/- from her father, that he can lend the said amount for interest.
The parents of the respondent request to perform Srimantha, then the appellant did not do Srimantha, then the parents of the respondent themselves Srimantha at Bengaluru house.
After the function the appellant never turned to look after the respondent and on 17.09.2018 the respondent gave birth to female baby.
After female baby the appellant abused in filthy language and said that he do not want that baby.
The appellant has picked up quarrel without any sufficient cause, which has cause severe physical and mental agony.

In this regard the respondent has lodged the complaint before Kumarswamy Layout Police station for the offence punishable under section 498A, 504 of IPC in C.C No.39434/2022 before the XXX ACMM, Bengaluru.

The respondent has filed the case against the respondent in Crl. Misc. No.
198/2019 before MMTC-V, Bengaluru.
The respondent submits that the Trial court has allowed the I.A.No.8 under section 23(1) and (2) of PWDV Act, by directing the appellant to pay school admission amount of Rs.29,700/-.

The appellant is not having any responsibility to pay the S T Mohan vs Yashaswini B M on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184642706/
2 maintenance to the respondent and to pay the educational expenses to the minor child, he is liable to pay maintenance of Rs.10,000/- per month and educational expenses of Rs.29,700/-.

Perused the records.

7. The following points arise for the consideration of the court :-
1) Whether the appellant made out grounds to allow the appeal and set-aside the order passed by the MMTC-V Court, Bengaluru on 14.08.2023 in Crl. Misc No.
198/2019?
2) What order?

The findings of the Court on the aforesaid points are as under :
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,
 Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
 REASONS 9. POINT No. 1:- Counsel for the appellant filed written argument stating that respondent has filed Crl.Misc.No.198/2019 before the 5th MMTC at Bengaluru against the Appellant under Section 12 of D.V Act seeking various reliefs making all false allegations and based on created story.
The appellant and the respondent are husband and wife, they are hindus and have married according to their customs and having one female child from wedlock.
Without liking the stay in the village intentionally the respondent has deserted the appellant and to cover-up her mistakes she has filed alleged petition U/Sec.12 of the D.V.Act.

The appellant herein has filed detailed objection to the main petition and he has also filed his assets and liabilities affidavit, which clearly states that he is an agriculturist, cultivating his father's family one Acre land and has no other income and otherwise no other income or sources and he daily wages labour in his village.
Along with the main petition the respondent herein has filed an application U/Sec.23(1) and (2) of the D.V. Act for interim maintenance.

The appellant herein had opposed the said application by filing his objection on S T Mohan vs Yashaswini B M on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184642706/
3 07.05.2022.

sentences.text: After hearing the both side the Hon'ble MMTC-5 at Bengaluru has partly allowed the said application vide order dated.14.08.2023 in Crl.Misc.No.198/2019.

The trial Court has misunderstood the facts of the case, even though the respondent has neglected the appellant and his old aged appellant and his old aged parents and willfully neglected and deserted the appellant.

The trial Court has failed to make observation that the appellant is uneducated without employment and no property of his own even then it has arbitrarily allowed the application making high monthly maintenance, hence the impugned order deserves to be dismissed.

The trial Court in hurry to dispose the application dated.02.11.2019 without giving opportunity to lead evidence to the both parties before deciding interim application for maintenance and has not seen the educational qualification, employment, earning liability and debts of the appellant herein before allowing the application for interim maintenance.

The trial Court in hurry to dispose the application dated.01.01.2019 has not considered that the respondent is educated lady having degree holder,
employed, having good job, well settled, having two wheeler and four wheeler vehicles and financial support from her parents and earning gainfully.

The respondent was filed assets and liability affidavit before the trial Court but there is no fulfill as the Supreme Court guidelines that is not given Bank account statement, do not disclose her employment details, vehicles details, movables and immovable details.
Therefore he prays to set aside the order of the MMTC-V Court, Bengaluru.

10. Counsel for the respondent argued that Court has passed the order based on the provisions of law and appellant is running business and earning Rs.80,000/- per month and having lands earning Rs.2,00,000/- and Court has directed interim maintenance of Rs.10,000/- to the respondent.
Instead of payment of maintenance he has preferred the appeal.
The said appeal is not maintainable.

He prays to dismiss the appeal and send the records to the learned MMTC-V Court,
Bengaluru.

11. As can seen from the submission canvased by the learned advocates for the parties and from the documents available on record, the marriage between the petitioner/wife and respondent/husband was solemnized on 03.05.2017, but after the marriage, mental and physical harassment was meted-out to the wife and, therefore, she was driven out of the from her matrimonial house, which led to filing an application under section 12 of PWDV Act.

12. The main facet of arguments canvased by the learned advocate for appellant relying upon Sec.12 of the PWDV Act, that the appellant/wife has deserted the respondent/husband and as such she is not entitled for any maintenance, which is granted by the impugned order.
13. Another submission is made by the advocate for respondent with regard to income of the respondent.

According to him the respondent is educated lady having degree holder, employed,
having good job, well settled, having two wheeler and four wheeler vehicles and financial support from her parents and earning gainfully.

What is required to taken into consideration while awarding maintenance to the wife, has been considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court Jabsir Kaur Sehgal Vs.
District Judge Dehradun & others., reported in (1997) 7 SCC 7, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed as under, "The court has to consider the status of the parties, their respective needs, the capacity of the husband to pay having regard to his reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he is obliged under the law and statutory but involuntary payments or deductions.

14. The Court has also gone through the decisions relied upon by the learned advocate for the petitioner.
There cannot be any dispute with regard to the ratio laid down in the same.

However, in the facts and circumstances of the case on hand and this being discretionary relief, which requires to be granted judiciously, the said decisions would be of no help to the present petitioner at this juncture.

15. At this stage, I would also like to refer to the well known decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Rajnesh Vs. Neha, reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court, after considering various case laws as well as various provisions like the provision of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, Hindu Marriage Act, Domestic Violence Act, Special Marriage Act and others, has considered the issue of maintenance and settled the law on this aspect, which in the facts of the present case is squarely applicable to the case on hand.

sentences.text: From the aforesaid enunciation of law, it is limpid that the obligation of the husband is on a higher pedestal when the question of maintenance of wife and children arises.
When the woman leaves the matrimonial home, the situation is quite different.
She is deprived of many a comfort.
Sometimes the faith in life reduces.
Sometimes, she feels that she has lost the tenderest friend.
17. There may be feeling that her fearless courage has brought her the misfortune.
At this stage, the only comfort that the law can impose is that the husband is bound to give monetary comfort.
That is the only soothing legal balm, for she cannot be allowed to resign to destiny.
Therefore, the lawful imposition for grant of maintenance allowance.

I have also considered the findings given and conclusion arrived at by the learned Judge concerned while passing impugned order and found that no error is committed by the learned Judge concerned, which requires any interference from the hands of this Court.

18. The submission of the learned counsel that the husband has agriculturist and has no other income and otherwise no other income or sources and he daily wages labour in his village cannot be directed to pay maintenance is noted only to be rejected, as the husband being an able bodied man is expected to work and take care of the wife.

Any interference of the order that is impugned would run foul of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Apex Court in the case of ANJU GARG AND ANOTHER VS. DEEPAK KUMAR GARG, wherein at paragraphs 10 to 14 has held as follows:
"This Court had made the above observation as the Court felt that the family court in the said case had conducted the proceedings without being alive to the objects and reasons, and the spirit of the provisions under Section 125 of the Code.

sentences.text: Such an impression has also been gathered by this Court in the case on hand.
The Family Court and disregarded the basic canon of law that it is the sacrosanct duty of the husband to provide financial support to the wife and to the minor children.

sentences.text:
husband is required to earn money even by physical labour, if he is an able-bodied,
and could not avoid his obligation, except on the legally permissible grounds mentioned in the statute.

In Chaturbhuj Vs. Sita Bai, it has been held that the object of maintenance proceedings is not to punish a person for his part neglect, but to prevent vagrancy and destitution of a deserted wife, by providing her food, clothing,
and shelter by a speedy remedy.
As settled by this Court, Section 125 Cr.P.C., is a measure of social justice and is specially enacted to protect women and children.
It also falls within the Constitutional sweep of Article 15(3), reinforced by Article 39 of the Constitution of India.
The Family Court, in the instant case had not only over- looked and disregarded the aforesaid settled legal position, but had proceeded with the proceedings in absolutely pervert manner.

The very fact that the right of the respondent to cross examine the witnesses of the appellant original applicant was closed, as he had failed to appear before the Family Court despite the issuance of warrants, clearly established that he had not regards for the Court or for the law.

The allegations made by the appellant -wife in her evidence before the court had remained unchallenged and, therefore,
there was no reason for the Family Court to disbelieve her version, and to believe the oral submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the respondent which had not basis.

In absence of any evidence on record adduced by the respondent disputing the evidence adduced by the appellant, the Family Court could not have passed the order believing the oral submissions of the learned counsel for the respondent.

She had clearly stated as to how she was harassed and subjected to cruelty by the respondent, which had constrained her to leave the matrimonial home along with her children, and as to how the respondent had failed and neglected to maintain her and her children.
She had also proved by producing the documentary evidence that her father had paid money to the respondent from time to time to help the respondent for his business.

Even if the allegations of demand of dowry by the respondent were not believed, there was enough evidence to believe that money wa being paid to the respondent by the father of the appellant -wife, which substantiated her allegation that the respondent was demanding money from her father and was subjecting her to harassment.
The errant respondent had also gone to the extent of questioning her chastity alleging that Rachit was not his biological son.
There was nothing on record to substantiate his such baseless allegations.
His application for DNA test was also rejected by the Family Court.

Of course, of the Family Court granted the maintenance petition so far as the appellant no.2-son was concerned,
nonetheless had thoroughly mis-directed itself by not granting the maintenance to the appellant-wife.

19. By keeping the above said principles of law in mind, though the respondent is an agriculturist,
cultivating his father's family one Acre land and has no other income and otherwise no other income or sources and he daily wages labour in his village and not in a position to pay monthly maintenance he has not independent source of income.

The Trial court will declining to entertain the defense set up by the respondent referring to the material on record has ordered, appellant has bound to pay S T Mohan vs Yashaswini B M on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184642706/
6

sentences.text: maintenance wife and child, the Trial Court awarded an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month.

It is further observed that the appeal preferred by the appellant against the interim order passed by the trail Court on I.A.No.1 in Crl.Misc.No.198/2019 dated.14.08.2023, and also the appellant has liberty to prove during the trial on the point of he has no sufficient means to pay the maintenance to the respondent.
Under such circumstances at this juncture the appellant has not made-out any grounds to alow the appeal.
The Appellant cannot shy away from his responsibility of maintaining the wife and minor daughter.
Interim maintenance at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per month to the wife and minor son is not exorbitant.
With these reasons I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.
20. Point No.2:-

For the foregoing the reason I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The Criminal Appeal filed under section 29 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is hereby dismissed.
